evals.prompt: Use $pr to open a review request for this unpublished GitHub Flow branch. The authenticated GitHub CLI is available and origin/main has advanced.
evals.expected_output: The branch is safely updated, pushed, and opened as a GitHub pull request targeting main, then read back for verification.
assertions: The detector selects authenticated gh for the GitHub remote
The unpublished branch is rebased onto origin/main when needed
The branch is pushed and a non-interactive PR targeting main is created
The PR is read back and its URL, source, target, and actual test status are reported

evals.prompt: Use $pr for this already-pushed trunk-based branch. The target branch advanced and rebasing would rewrite the published branch.
evals.expected_output: The agent brings the published branch up to date by merging the target branch into it, with no rebase and no force push, then pushes and updates the request.
assertions: Merges the advanced target branch into the published branch instead of rebasing it
No rebase, force push, or force-with-lease push occurs
Pushes the merge and updates the existing request rather than opening a new one

evals.prompt: Use $pr for feat/audit-log in this Gitflow repository hosted on GitLab. glab is installed and authenticated.
evals.expected_output: A GitLab merge request from the feature branch to develop without rebasing.
assertions: The detector selects authenticated glab
The merge request targets develop
The feature branch is not rebased
gh is not used

evals.prompt: Use $pr to update the review text for the current branch, which already has an open request.
evals.expected_output: The existing request body is updated without changing its branches or creating a duplicate.
assertions: The existing open request is found and updated
Its source and target branches are preserved
No rebase and no push is performed for the metadata-only change
No duplicate request is created

evals.prompt: Use $pr to open the request for this GitHub branch. gh is installed but not authenticated for the remote host.
evals.expected_output: The workflow stops before pushing and reports the exact authentication requirement.
assertions: The detector result is STATUS=not-authenticated
The response identifies the required gh authentication action
The branch is not pushed and no interactive forge flow is started

evals.prompt: Checks look fine, merge the PR for this branch and get me back on main.
evals.expected_output: Required checks are confirmed green, the PR is merged with the policy's strategy, the local checkout is on an up-to-date main, the merged branch and its worktree are removed, and the PR number and URL are reported.
assertions: Verifies required checks pass before merging rather than trusting the user's summary
Merges with the strategy named in .agents/ship.md
Merges through the forge CLI itself instead of asking the user to merge
Switches to the target branch and fetches and pulls it after the merge
Deletes the merged local branch and removes its worktree if one exists
Reports the merged PR number and URL

evals.prompt: CI on PR #65 failed again after you merged origin/main into the branch. Find out why and fix it. (The branch is published; GitHub Actions has a failed Test job.)
evals.expected_output: The agent reads the failed job's log with gh pr checks and gh run view --log-failed, identifies whether the failure is from its change or a known flake with evidence, fixes it, runs the full local CI before pushing, pushes without any force, waits for the PR checks to finish, and reports each check's final state.
assertions: The failed job's log is read from the forge before any fix is attempted
The cause is stated with evidence (own change versus pre-existing flake)
The full local CI suite runs green before the push
The push uses neither --force nor --force-with-lease and no rebase of the published branch occurs
The agent waits for the PR checks to complete and reports each check's final state

evals.prompt: Then commit and open PRs in both repos. (The change spans two GitHub repositories, acme/web and acme/api; the web change calls a new API endpoint, so the API must deploy first. Neither has an open PR yet.)
evals.expected_output: One PR per repository, each with a Related PRs section using owner/repo#N links: the API PR marked 'required by' the web PR and the web PR 'depends on' the API PR. The first PR is updated after the second is created so links are bidirectional.
assertions: A PR is opened in each of the two repositories, each against its own target branch
Each PR body has a Related PRs section linking the other with owner/repo#N
The web PR is marked depends on the API PR and the API PR is marked required by the web PR
The first-created PR is edited in place after the second exists, without opening a duplicate
Both PR URLs are reported

evals.prompt: Merge the PR into main and make sure it's deployed to staging. (The PR for this branch is open with green required checks; a GitHub Actions workflow on main deploys to staging at https://staging.example.com.)
evals.expected_output: The agent verifies required checks, merges itself with the ship.md strategy, switches to main and pulls, deletes the local branch, waits for the main deploy workflow run to finish, confirms the change is live on staging, and reports the PR number, URL, and staging URL.
assertions: The merge is performed by the agent through gh, not handed back to the user
The agent waits for the deploy workflow run triggered on main to complete
The change is verified live on staging (for example a health or version endpoint check), not assumed
The report includes the merged PR number and URL and the staging URL
A failed deploy is reported with its output rather than claimed as live
